verified_entityos_binary.head_note: Current product head 4c2607d only adds a source-admitted ClayVM test workflow; no EntityOS product source mutation relative to parent b32ec5d was observed, but the verified binary remains build-head-bound to b32ec5d and is not relabeled as an exact 4c2607d build.

upstream_sqlite.finding: SQLite upstream documents the WAL-reset corruption bug as affecting versions 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and as fixed in 3.51.3; upstream also names backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.

grf.hypothesis: The accepted target's stock SQLite 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7 cannot currently satisfy the EntityOS persistence release gate because neither exact runtime trust anchoring nor evidence of the upstream WAL-reset fix is present.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: Ubuntu may have carried an equivalent fix under a differently named patch or source delta not detected by changelog/series heuristics.
grf.discriminating_evidence: Exact loaded-library identity plus installed changelog and published Ubuntu source patchset were checked independently; neither package nor published patchset supplied explicit WAL-reset evidence, while upstream marks 3.45.1 inside the affected version range.
grf.promotion_scope: release blocker evidence; does not by itself prove every possible downstream-equivalent patch absent

next_executable_step: Choose and execute one release-safe persistence route: preferably make the one-file EntityOS load a fixed SQLite runtime whose upstream/base version is >=3.51.3 (or an explicitly proven fixed backport), bind runtime source/build identity plus loaded-library SHA-256 into a non-bypassable trust anchor, reject downgrade/library swap, then rerun the productive-path, package/source provenance, crash/restart/WAL lifecycle, and canonical one-file EntityOS gates on the accepted Ubuntu target. If retaining host-dynamic SQLite instead, upgrade the accepted target to an equivalently proven fixed build before minting the anchor. Do not promote 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7 on current evidence.
